[[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] (2013–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Sporting News|TSN]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2015]]) * [[Pacific-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] ([[2014–15 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2015]]) * First-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2015) * Second-team All-Pac-12 ([[2013–14 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2014]]) * Third-team All-Conference USA (2013) * Conference USA All-Freshman (2012) * Third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2010) | medal_templates = }} '''Joseph Michael Young''' (born June 27, 1992) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. As a senior in 2014–15, the [[guard (basketball)|guard]] was named the [[Pacific-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pacific-12 Conference Player of the Year]].{{cite news|last=Alger|first=Tyson|title=Dana Altman and Joseph Young named Pac-12's coach and player of the year|date=March 9, 2015|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2015/03/dana_altman_and_joseph_young_n.html|accessdate=March 9, 2015}} He is the son of former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] player [[Michael Young (basketball)|Michael Young]].{{cite web|title=Joseph Young Bio|work=uhcougars.com|url=http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_joseph00.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuQiUmYo|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}} Joseph Young originally committed to [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], but was forced to sit out a season after fired head coach [[Keno Davis]] refused to release him from his letter of intent. He began his collegiate career at [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], where his father was Director of Basketball Operations. As a sophomore, Young scored 18 points per game and shot 42 percent from the three point arc and 87 percent on free throws. After the season, Michael Young refused reassignment at the University of Houston and left the program, and his son opted to transfer.{{cite news|last1=Phillips|first1=Scott|title=Houston leading scorer Joseph Young, and father Michael, leaving the program|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/06/01/houston-leading-scorer-joseph-young-and-father-michael-leaving-the-program/|accessdate=June 7, 2015|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=June 1, 2013}} He announced his transfer to Oregon to play under coach [[Dana Altman]].{{cite news|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Oregon lands guard Joseph Young|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9433570/houston-cougars-transfer-joseph-young-lands-oregon-ducks|accessdate=June 7, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=June 28, 2013}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{commons-inline}} *[http://www.goducks.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209278100 Oregon Ducks bio] *[http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_joseph00.html Houston Cougars bio] {{Pacific-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{Persondata | NAME = Young, Joseph | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Young, Joseph}} [[Category:1992 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Texas]] [[Category:Guards (basketball)]] [[Category:Houston Cougars men's basketball players]] [[Category:Oregon Ducks men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Houston, Texas]] {{1990s-US-basketball-bio-stub}}
